w:r.w:t: Use this section to highlight your most impressive achievements with specific numbers or measurable results. Focus on how your skills and experience created real value for previous projects or teams. Avoid writing about what you want—instead, show employers exactly how you can help their company succeed.
Begin by clearly defining your role’s main focus or challenge to provide context for your achievements.
Briefly describe your environment or scale, such as team size or market reach, to add depth to experience.
Highlight promotions, leadership, or major projects to show growth and credibility.
Emphasize measurable results — like growth, savings, or performance gains.
Use action verbs like led, improved, implemented, or developed — avoid passive phrasing.
Focus on results and achievements, not duties; quantify them when possible (%, $, or numbers).
Arrange your bullet points strategically — put the most relevant and impressive accomplishments first.
Proofread carefully — errors or formatting issues can harm first impressions.
Use a professional tone and layout; keep it clean, modern, and easy to read for both humans and ATS.
Review your résumé in 10 seconds — the top achievements should immediately stand out.
